Inherent becoming and inherent destruction can't coexist in the same entity at the same instant.","quantum":"Complementarity principle (Bohr): wave and particle aspects can't be observed simultaneously — they're complementary but mutually exclusive in any given measurement. Like v.2: becoming and destruction are complementary (v.1) but mutually exclusive (v.2).","bridge":"Both Bohr's complementarity and v.2 show mutually dependent yet mutually exclusive aspects. They're opposite directions. Similarly: becoming (arising) and destruction (ceasing) can't happen simultaneously in the same thing.","twoTruths":"Conventionally: we observe sequential becoming and destruction — things arise, then later cease. Ultimately: neither the sequence nor the simultaneity can be inherent.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying things can't change rapidly. Conventional change involves rapid sequences of arising and ceasing. Similarly, an entity can't be simultaneously arising and ceasing."},{"q":"Why does the birth/death analogy work?","a":"Birth and death are the most vivid examples of becoming and destruction.
